audit.whatIsWrong: diff said EVEN at 6/10 while the Emerald+ win rate is 46.17% over 431 games, and the level chart gave Level 1 to Irelia and Level 3 to Singed — both backwards, and both contradicted by the page's own whys text (whys[0] describes Singed denying her a target; whys[2] calls Level 3 'the lone window that's yours').
audit.why: The mirror audit on singed__irelia already flipped Level 1 to Singed and Level 3 to Irelia as one atomic group and set that page to 4/10 FAV. Irelia's side must be the inverse: 7/10, UNFAV, same two rows flipped in both layers.
audit.corrected: diff UNFAV, diffRating 7/10, difficulty and final-rating rows matched; win[0]/phases[0].side to Singed with rating 4/10, win[2]/phases[2].side to Irelia with rating 7/10, proposed as one group with both whys rewritten to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: Cooldown advice was entirely abstract — 'his flip, bait it, then stun', 'your committal tool', 'your ultimate' — with zero numbers anywhere on the page (packet sequencingCues: 0). Mega Adhesive was never named as a cooldown at all.
audit.why: Fling is E on 10/9.5/9/8.5/8, Mega Adhesive is W on 17/16/15/14/13, Vanguard's Edge is 125/105/85. Those are the three timers the lane is actually played around.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, report[5].t and spikes[2].text now carry the real numbers: Fling 10s at rank 1, Mega Adhesive 17s, Vanguard's Edge 125s.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three separate ability errors. (a) Fling was repeatedly slotted as (W) — 'get Flung (W)', 'after he Flings (W)', 'Fling you (W)'. Fling is E; W is Mega Adhesive. (b) Defiant Dance was credited with soaking Poison Trail in mid, late and spikes[3] — its damage reduction is physical only and Poison Trail is magic damage, so the page told the player to tank poison with a filter that does not apply to it. (c) Mega Adhesive's grounding appeared nowhere on the page, even though it is the single interaction that decides the matchup: it shuts Bladesurge off, and a Fling that lands in the glue roots as well.
audit.why: Irelia's own kit file flags Bladesurge as 'mobility that grounding and walls can deny', and Singed's W carries the grounding flag. Riot's W text confirms the root on a Fling landing in the adhesive. Riot's Defiant Dance text says 'reduced physical damage'. The mirror audit reached the same three conclusions from Singed's side.
audit.corrected: Fling re-slotted to (E) everywhere; Defiant Dance restated as physical-only with poison burning straight through it; Mega Adhesive grounding written into early, breakdown.cooldowns, breakdown.difficulty, report[5].t, dontsFull[1].d and wants.foe[1]. Also added the missing-interaction finding: Insanity Potion (R, 100s) makes Poison Trail apply Grievous Wounds, halving Bladesurge's heal — and the page had it exactly inverted, prescribing Executioner's Calling for 'his healing'.

audit.whatIsWrong: report[8].t prescribed Executioner's Calling early because 'his healing fights your pattern'. Singed has no heal in his kit; the anti-heal in this lane runs the other direction.
audit.why: Insanity Potion (R) makes Poison Trail apply Grievous Wounds to Irelia, cutting Bladesurge's sustain.
audit.corrected: Anti-heal line replaced with the real interaction in report[8].t and breakdown.late.

audit.why: suspectNames flagged 'Defiant Dance' as a probable wrong name. It is Irelia's real W name — a false positive from the near-miss matcher. The error in that sentence was the physical-only damage reduction claim, not the name.
audit.corrected: Name left as-is; the surrounding claim corrected.

edits.before: Singed's whole early game is to deny you a target — he proxies behind your wave and clears it with Poison Trail (Q), so your Bladesurge has no friendly minion to dash and reset off and your E-stun has no Singed body to land on. Don't chase him into the poison; you'll eat the cloud, get Flung (W) back toward his tower, and lose the trade to a champion you never actually touched. At level 3 with E up, the one time he steps to your wave his Fling is single-target while your E is a two-blade stun his move speed can't escape — Bladesurge the E-marked target for the reset, but punish only that.

edits.before: This is the closest thing you get to owning the lane: at 6, Vanguard's Edge is the textbook answer to a kiter. If he commits to a Fling, drop the blade wall behind him so he can't run-and-poison away, then E-stun and chain Bladesurge resets while Defiant Dance's damage reduction soaks the poison ticks. The problem is he rarely commits — he'd rather proxy and waveclear, so your power spike often has no one to spike on. Track him, set up with your jungler, and cash in the level-6 window hard, because it's the last point where you cleanly out-damage him.

edits.before: Once Singed has Rylai's and Liandry's he stops caring about your duel — the Fling-into-poison run-down becomes unkiteable, his massive HP/mana sustain out-lasts the chip your resets and passive armor shred deal, and he just walks at you through Defiant Dance's damage reduction. You can't reliably catch a champion whose entire kit is built to never be caught, and he'll proxy-split a side lane while your team 4v5s. Cash your level-6 and first-item tempo into towers and objectives early; if the game goes long, stop trying to solo-kill him and group to end before his scaling and splitpush take over the map.
